text_fidelity_a: Hauck Fire Rescue Pedal Go Kart Overall, I would say that I like the finished product of this kart, but the process wasn't the most pleasant. The directions are terrible--that was the worst part of the item. The directions are small pictures, with smaller pictures of items and the labeled part letter and numbers, making it hard to see. For example, there are nuts that have to be screwed onto the wheels and the picture is so small that you cannot see which end of the nut should go on the outside/ inside. I had to look very hard and make the best guess. Also, there are no words. I truly prefer words and pictures with directions so that I am clear especially for something that my child will be riding on. However, despite all of that the item is sturdy, looks good, and rides well. I put the seat on the last holes for my 5 year old (almost 6) who is 4' tall and it works well for him. However, I dont think any kid too much taller would be able to ride it comfortably. His legs are a little bent, and I dont see a kid up to 8 being able to ride this comfortably. It does ride over all kinds of surfaces, if they are flat or downhill. My son rode on flat grass (not the easiest but it did go), over rocks and concrete and it worked. Also the brake works very well, stops everytime even while going downhill.
text_fidelity_b: Hauck Fire Rescue Pedal Go Kart

Those good looks come out in the packaging, which wasn't too painful to extract the dragon from. You will need a screwdriver and C batteries to bring it to life. Boy does it come to life. The "fire breathing" effect works well, though with caveats . For starters it needs water to create the effect and that means distilled water, filters, and refills. All in all it works.

It's a little rough around the edges if you're looking to critique the toy, but kids love it, as does the kid all of us.

My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike [[VIDEOID:4ac7ba54c290a47a623bdcdbf7740f53]] This is an excellent My Little Pony doll and puppy. At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form
-Twilight Sparkle can't stand on her own, but this is typical for dolls like this

They did build a couple of the ideas in the book and we all found it interesting that Klutz combined paper elements into their Lego constructions. My kids are somewhat snobby purists so they were not really for it, but I think it is a great idea for more open-minded and younger builders.

Most of the builds are simple science tricks like making a strobing slot movie machine or a spinning image that also strobes when you spin it to blend images. text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Split Speeders Blade Raid Action Track Set This hot wheel set suffers from a similar issue to many other hot wheels sets we have tried: it doesn't hook up well with other hot wheels sets, most parts aren't interchangeable even when they look like they should be, and the action of the intended set will likely only be fun for a few days of play before becoming an oversized dust catcher.

I'm a big fan of the hot wheels sets that you can extend with other parts and enjoy in multiple ways. This set, the main launcher and the orange tracks can be used with normal cars and other sets. But obviously the splitter parts can only be used with the one car they give you.

I will say that it is more fun than the last hot wheels set we brought home, which is a closed system in which none of the parts can be used in any other way, and the action of it was lackluster. This set, at least sending the car through the tracks and launching it with the launcher is really cool.

A few of the parts look kind of flimsy, for example there are a few parts that move and function only because of skinny rubber bands that are visible and obvious on the back. I'm not sure I want teeny rubber bands in the same part of the house as a toddler, and i don't see why they couldn't enclose that area or use better parts.

Overall, I feel like this set is going to be really fun for a few days until part of the splitter car is lost, and then I'll harvest what parts we can use with normal cars and move on. It would be a decent choice to perk up a holiday gathering and be fun for a short time, but it packs staying power.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Split Speeders Blade Raid Action Track Set

Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets This is a redesign of previous Track Builder Loop Kicker, and it does same job - a rubber band powered leg gets triggered by car passing through to "kick" the car faster through the loop - but this one changes the pieces. Gone is the ball-joint of the center tower track mount from the older version (mount is still there, but fixed to flat position), and the 2 track pieces and center connector that make up the loop have been replaced by 2 fixed, hinged pieces of pre-curved plastic that snap together. Redesign comes with 2 less pieces of flat track.

Pros
- Kicker loop quicker to assemble than previous version
- Loop doesn't flex as much as old version, so cars keep more speed through the loop
- Includes 2 pieces of straight, low-sidewall track
- Includes 4 newest track connector pieces despite not needing any
- Includes 1 car that works with track (not all Hot Wheels work with all track sets)
- Kicker leg has a safety hinge so a second car can pass under it

Neutral
- The included car is an easily-found 2019 basic release, the mint Speed Blur series version of Exotique

Cons
- Isn't that much faster than just setting up or taking down track
- When folded down, takes up more space than the older one where you disassembled track
- Not that easy to remove the center tower from the base
- Smaller base is harder to put weights on to keep the track from moving when it kicks
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets

LEGO Friends Roller Disco Arcade Set 41708, Toy Bowling Game, Andrea Mini-Doll Included, Birthday Present Idea for Kids, Girls and Boys 7+, Fun Playset for Creative Play I’m actually old enough to remember disco night at the roller skating rink, so the Lego Friends Roller Disco Arcade set was a fun trip into nostalgia for me. The set is packed with cute details, bright colors, and play features. It might be the best Friends set I’ve ever built.

The disco arcade has 3 areas: the roller disco, the bowling lane (6 pins), and the arcade. The different areas are connected with hinges, so the set opens and closes. When it’s closed, the translucent green windows let you see inside the arcade. When it’s open, you can utilize all the different play areas without being cramped.

I really like how the building is designed to open and close! It looks cool either way. And if I compare this to a set that has an open back to access the play features, the roller rink just looks more complete.

I don’t love all the stickers, but for once I’m not going to ding the set. It would be impossible to print so many tiles. I do recommend adults help with sticker application, but the rest of the set is easily doable by a kid (6+). The instructions are clear as always with Lego. Pieces are separated into numbered bags to help with assembly (less time searching for the needed piece for a step) and to cut down slightly on mess while building.

Overall, I was really impressed by this set. It’s fun to build, fun to play with, and fun to have on display.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Friends Roller Disco Arcade Set 41708, Toy Bowling Game, Andrea Mini-Doll Included, Birthday Present Idea for Kids, Girls and Boys 7+, Fun Playset for Creative Play

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set This is a great set to introduce kids (as well as adults) to the art of latch hooking. The instruction book is colorful and easy to follow, with clear directions and beautiful graphics. I would give this a five-star review except for two things:

The book gets you and your child excited to start making beautiful projects (including your own customized designs), yet it provides only enough yarn and canvas to make ONE double-sided, child-size pillow. If you want to make bigger and more complicated projects, you have to order more supplies. Because of this, I felt this was more of a "sample" kit, aimed at giving newcomers a "taste" of latch hooking to get you "hooked." For $30, I expected enough material to make at least two projects. Also, what yarn there is of so-so quality - it's rather light and thin, "play yarn" for children, I guess.

Also the packaging felt odd. The book is tied to an empty cardboard box that seems to have no function other than to fill space to make the kit look bigger and more substantial than it is. It's tied so tightly with pipe cleaners that you can't help but tear the back of the book as you try to free it. Another reviewer commented that this may be due to craft stores experiencing a lot of shoplifting - but the book could have been easily secured using double sided tape or light adhesive.

Other than that, this kit will provide hours of enjoyment for adults and kids, especially those (like me) suffering from cabin fever thanks to an interminably long winter. I would definitely buy more as gifts if it were less than the current price.

text_fidelity_a:
SwimWays Paddle Paws Spring Float Dog Raft, Large (65 lbs. and Up), Blue This isn't really the proper review as I just received this product yesterday, but I did want to point something out for others maybe thinking of this product so they can get a fuller vision of it.

1st - it came ridiculously fast so shipping = excellent. I purchased on the Sunday before Memorial day and received the item the following Wed. afternoon with Amazon's Super Saver free shipping.

And now to the product -

Obviously I'll have to update this review with durability, but for now I can say that I took my dog out on it yesterday (the day we got it) and her monster-claws (that need a serious trim which she will receive today!!) didn't even phase this thing.

The part that's concerning me about this product is just how much water the dog sits in while floating. My dog LOVES water and so of the two choices of dog-float that Amazon offers I figured this was the better choice because the other one doesn't look like the dog gets wet at all and I figured that would get pretty hot for the pup. And even though there are many good pics for this item, I guess I was still envisioning that the dog would be floating with maybe an inch or two of water in the bottom - just enough to keep her cooled down. That's not the case. For my 100# girl, she is laying in about 4-5 inches of water at all times. Cooling? yes, but comfortable? I'm thinking no, not for a dog; at least not for any real length of time. Buyers should be aware that the pic with the Portuguese Water Dog (that I thought was only THAT full of water because the dog is laying over the edge of the float) is a perfectly accurate pic of just how much water the dog will be sitting in at all times while on this float.

In the future hopefully someone will come out with a product that offers just a little LESS contact with the water to create a more perfect balance of cooling and comfort for the dog.

UPDATE: So I actually purchased this for a tubing trip that the dog was going to come along on, which we did this weekend.

End result for this product: The river was super low so we had a LOT of the dog jumping in and out as we'd hit rocks, a LOT of dragging over long distances of rocks, and some fast moving water - over endless rocks! lol I know this wasn't the intention of this product but as far as any 'ripping' there was absolutely none - and we couldn't have put this thing through it's paces any more than that river trip was!! But as far as the durability of the small ring that makes this hold it's shape - that broke just while refolding the item and I learned quickly how important that was within about 30 minutes on the river. :( The product won't hold it's shape very well at all without it. Oh, also, the air stopper kept randomly coming open and not due to the rocks, just whenever, even in calm water. So that was a problem too.

As speculated in the original review, the dog did NOT like being in that much water for an extended amount of time, AND the fabric seemed to almost stretch out a bit because she sat lower and lower (in more water) the longer we were on the river.

Now, all that said, in a pool, I think this product would do just fine - where the dog could get out whenever it got sick of laying in so much water - but I still do think the plastic ring will snap in a heart beat just due to regular un/folding, and needs to be rethought by the manufacturer.
text_fidelity_b: SwimWays Paddle Paws Spring Float Dog Raft, Large (65 lbs. and Up), Blue

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.

Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

It's a lot harder than it first appears.  You need to work together to gather the treasures before the island sinks, and once it starts sinking, it just keeps sinking faster, first because as the water level rises you draw more cards, and each card means a section sinks a bit more, and second because once a section sinks you take its card out of play, spreading the increasing damage to a decreasing area.  You can set the difficulty, but even on the easiest setting, it's a challenge for first time players.  This is fast becoming my favorite cooperative tabletop game.  Fans of Pandemic will enjoy this. LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

UPDATE—7/1118
We’ve had our new leapstart book (this time I bought at big box store with a warranty) for 5 months now since the last broke, so far so good but I’m still not sure on longevity still, however i have changed batteries a few times since we use ours alot and have had no issues. I am adding a star as my kids fight over this all the time. I’ve got 6yo boy who LOVES it who is also my reader and 4yo girl who always wants what her brother has but genuinely love this thing. I struggle with getting my kids to play with their $100 toy they got for Christmas but love this thing and it’s a plus for me since it’s educational. So i still can’t give this item as high of a star as I would like because of durability I would recommend it if you don’t care if you have to replace it. I’m glad I did but recommend getting some warranty because after investing in the books and how much my kids like It, you may want to get another.

Snap Circuits Jr. SC-100 Electronics Exploration Kit, Over 100 Projects, Full Color Project Manual, 28 Snap Circuits Parts, STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8 + [[VIDEOID:17092331]]This is the ideal kit to get your child on the road to understanding electricity. Everything just snaps together like building blocks, and there's no need for screwdrivers, soldering irons, electrical tape or testers.

The instruction manual is easy to read, and includes diagrams for 101 projects. With a little help for the first few, a child can easily work their way through the book with minimal adult supervision.

The video shows a few of the projects - a switch circuit with light bulb, running a DC motor and fan, a Space War alarm combo, and a flying saucer. There's also a clip of a lamp and fan in series, showing that the fan takes a while to turn at full speed because of inertia.

There are also games, sirens, projects activated by clapping or light, and projects that introduce digital circuits. There are three kits that are more advanced, but you can also get upgrade kits to take each to the next level.

If you're looking for an educational toy that your child will really enjoy, I recommend you put this one on your list.

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces This retails for about $30. At that price I think it's a great little toy and highly giftable. For whatever reason the price is crazy high on Amazon at the time of this review (about double the retail price). It is not worth nearly $70. That is just crazy.

Going with the retail value, I will review it as a $30 toy.

It does feel a bit flimsy with how the pieces snap in and out of the arena. You may need to help younger kids, and it's best if you really do try to line up the teenie tiny triangle on each piece with the triangle printed on the arena piece. Makes it much easier to snap your fighter in. Also, make sure you cut off the plastic rubber band harnessed around each fighter. Otherwise they are invincible, that was a fun discovery when kiddo went undefeated and we realized it was because his guy couldn't die.

Speaking of kiddo, my son is 9 and LOVES this thing. I was bored in about 10min, but I'm guessing mid-40s mom is not the target demographic. My husband had a bit more fun, and those two really got crazy with it. There does seem to be some technique involved, past just smashing into each other until someone wins. But hey, its how I played Street Fighter back in the 80s, and mashing all the buttons is how I play Akedo in 2021.

Also, the numbers on the pieces for offense and defense are pointless. Some fighters are just better, there isn't any way around it. The defensive pieces usually just mean you will never land an attack and are pointless.

TL;DR: for the $30 the kid loves it. I could see this being a popular birthday party gift.
text_fidelity_b: Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces

Blue Orange Ring It! The Clap & Ring Game I love games that can manage parity across many ages. This is a lot like Spot it in that regards, where a 7 year old can compete fairly well with a 47 year old once everyone knows what they are looking for. The reaching for the bell is kinetic enough to engage kids to make them want to be the first to slam the ringer, and the rules are so easy they can immediately be digested. The action is fast and again engaging, and we had a lot of laughs with the came, and surprisingly few injuries and fights.

The game in its simplest form is almost too easy, but it lends itself to more and more levels of complexity. There are three variables, numbers, color (8 or more) and a shape. You can play complex combos like match a shape and a number, or two numbers must add up to ten and there needs to be a match. Instant ring it and visually similar don't ring it cards cause quick victories as well as quick penalties.

This is a perfect game to pull out for some quick games. The container holds all the pieces and makes it wonderfully portable. The parts are decent quality and I expect it to hold up well.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Ring It! The Clap & Ring Game

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf N-Strike Elite Rapidstrike CS-18 Blaster (Colors may vary) My kids have had an absolute blast with this nerf firearm. I am amazed at the speed that it empties an 18 dart clip with startling accuracy. I am also impressed at the decent but manageable sting that the darts give you when your tween son unloads on you.

The construction seems very solid. It is amazing that it has sensors that will not allow firing when the chamber is open or the clip is missing. There are lock release buttons on everything from stock extension to a safety for firing (well maybe more just a button to engage the fly wheel more than a safety.) Also there are rails for accessories and clip loops for attaching a carrying strap. Perhaps the most superfluous feature is the fold down sight. I have never seen my boys aim. It seems to favor firing from the hip.

Pros
+ Absolute blast to fire
+ Satisfying click when slamming the clip home
+ Impressive accuracy
+ Well Constructed

Cons
- It does Jam, especially when trying to use the clips from other guns in the series.
- Bullets seem to burrow to freedom after shooting them, or turn invisible because they just disappear.
- Needs 4 C batteries
- Having just one causes sibling bickering

I do find it funny that they rate this for educational purposes. But I guess it is a great introduction into our gun culture. The false sense of strength and self confidence it provides is very self evident as you fire down on someone with only a pump action nerf gun, or better yet, an unarmed victim. We have lost a lot of darts in a short time, but that's what supplemental dart packs are for.

I feel like I'm putting in too many cons, because In the words of my boys, "This thing is awesome." I wish they had these when I was their age. Either that or I wish the office had a more lax view on noon-time Nerf battles.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Rapidstrike CS-18 Blaster (Colors may vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive) The Barbies in my day were just ridiculously shaped, so much so that even in the third grade I rejected them as a model that I would never live up to in my own feminine figure. I remember wishing that I could play with Barbies, but the body shapes made me feel unhappy and inadequate – you might think girls aren't aware of this kind of thing at a young age, but I certainly was. I owned one or two, but they were never something I love for this reason.

So just imagine my delight to realize that Barbie has created so many interesting and diverse dolls now to play with. This Daisy figure has really just a normal kind of shape that you would see on many, many ladies and moms at the grocery store. She looked beautiful, and also has a much more realistic form. I love the styling of her outfit, and her gorgeous pink hair just straight up makes me happy to look at and brush.

The way that they chose to craft Barbies slightly bigger thighs was interesting to me, so I took a photo of it. Overall, this feels like a really body positive, average pretty Barbie to play with, who is stylish and fun and attractive yet doesn't set up my daughter with completely ridiculous ideas of what women might look like.

Even the normal Barbies, I have a chicken farmer Barbie, and a Barbie who runs a doggy daycare, seem like their proportions have evolved somewhat, and then the fact that they are doing normal things like cleaning up dog messes and collecting eggs really goes so far in my book. I also love the Ken doll who is doing his own laundry in his very own washing machine. My husband is a little flummoxed by my absolute flat out glee at seeing such a thing, but I think setting the expectation that Ken will enjoy doing his own self-care chores is an excellent one for young ladies.

Overall, from having the impression that I would never let my children play with Barbies, I've come a long way, and that's because Barbie has come a long way to. I'm delighted with Daisy, and her cool accessories and great look.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive)

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. They have additional kits over here [[ASIN:B01CL1FCEY 3Doodler Start Rocket & Robot DoodleBlock Kit]] not just the robot, but a page full of them, if you get tired of hexbugs.
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold
